headline: Single-cell QTL mapping resolves cell-type and temporal control of gene regulation
label: Genetic Variant Association Mapping
summary: Expanded single-cell, tandem repeat, and circadian eQTL datasets now enable cell-type and time-resolved variant effect mapping at scale.
synthesis: The common thread is genetic association analysis moving beyond bulk, single-variant effect estimates toward cell-type- and time-resolved resolution. TenK10K phase 1 maps common and rare variant effects on immune gene expression across 28 cell types in over 5 million single cells, and a scATAC-seq study of 3.5M PBMCs from 1,042 donors maps caQTLs, with a graph neural network linking peaks to genes using QTL layers. Tandem repeat variation is tied to cell-type-specific expression and chromatin across 1.7M repeats in 5.4M immune cells. Genotype-by-rhythm cosinor analysis of GTEx v10 identifies 167 circadian eQTLs across 28 tissues, extending QTL mapping to temporal regulation. Complementary resources (scMRdb for cell-type-resolved Mendelian randomization, VarNexus for regulatory variant interpretation, MetabDB and MetabHub for metabolic QTL and GWAS integration) and a reproducible CADD-annotated pipeline built from GWAS summary statistics extend these analyses to interpretation and prediction. What is new is explicit cell-type and temporal resolution of QTL effects.
